workload.description: 20k player req/s (~72k concurrent streams); 90% are CDN segment fetches

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: m6i.large — AWS EC2 us-east-1 / On-Demand / Linux / shared tenancy / 730 h per month; instance-hour only (excludes EBS, data transfer); x86-64 (Intel Ice Lake). Band: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Month length (672-744 h), burstable credit surcharges, Savings Plans and Spot are OUT-OF-BAND modifiers, named per row, not band edges.

citations.note: $0.096/h x 730 = 7008c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117).

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: cache.r6g.large — AWS ElastiCache us-east-1 / On-Demand / Redis engine / standard support / 730 h per month; node-hour only. Band: zero-width at the Redis/Memcached standard-support rate. The Valkey engine is CHEAPER and Extended Support is DEARER; both are different products/support states, not a price range for this row, so they are named here rather than used as band edges.

db.m6i.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.178/h Single-AZ x 730 = 12994c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class.

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: kafka.t3.small — AWS MSK us-east-1 / On-Demand / provisioned broker / 730 h per month; broker-hour only (excludes storage and data transfer). Band: zero-width: single published broker-hour rate in the pinned scope.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 20,000 player requests/s at peak. 90% are 4-second HLS/DASH segment fetches, which at 0.25 segments/s per stream is ~72,000 concurrent streams. Manifest/start, catalogue browse and ingest share the remaining 10%.

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: Edge cache hit-rate 98% on segments — the head of a VOD catalogue is small and hot, so only 2% of segment requests reach the origin. Contracted edge capacity ~26,000 segment req/s (~300 Gbps at 1.5 MB per segment). A CDN's real capacity is elastic and contractual, not an instance count; treat this row as the contract you bought, not a machine you own.

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: THE COST LESSON, stated plainly: this architecture is a BYTES problem, not a requests problem. Delivered segment traffic is roughly 68 PB/month (18,000 seg/s x 1.5 MB). That volume is NOT in the bill below, because it is bought on a committed CDN contract at rates 10-30x under the model's flat $0.09/GB internet rate, and pricing it at the flat rate would overstate the bill by an order of magnitude. What IS priced is the metered origin->edge fill: 2% of 68 PB = ~1.37 PB/month. Compute is a rounding error next to either figure.

assumptions.subject: store
assumptions.statement: Object-store capacity 5,500 GET/s, the documented S3 per-prefix ceiling; renditions are laid out under one prefix at this request rate. Storage 500 TB = a ~50,000-title catalogue at 5 ABR renditions each.

assumptions.subject: app
assumptions.statement: The control plane is genuinely small: only ~2,000 rps of API traffic sits behind 20,000 rps of player traffic, because the segment path never touches an app server. 3 instances is multi-AZ redundancy, not a throughput requirement.

assumptions.subject: q
assumptions.statement: Transcode ingest is ~10 uploads/s, so the job bus runs at a fraction of a percent. It is 3 brokers for replication-factor-3 durability — losing a transcode job list is worse than paying for idle brokers.

assumptions.subject: engine
assumptions.statement: Transcoding itself is a BATCH workload (minutes of GPU/CPU per title) and is not modelled: the engine sizes request-serving components against a per-second arrival rate, and a transcode farm is sized against a backlog-drain deadline instead. The queue row here models job submission only.

_library.summary: VOD platform where a CDN absorbs 90% of traffic as segment fetches and a small control plane serves manifests, catalogue and ingest.
